documents.citation: Excerpt from Martin Luther King Jr., speech delivered at the first mass meeting of the Montgomery Improvement Association, Holt Street Baptist Church, Montgomery, Alabama, December 5, 1955. Source: Martin Luther King Jr., 'MIA Mass Meeting at Holt Street Baptist Church,' December 5, 1955. The text of this speech is in the public record as preserved in movement archives and reported in The Montgomery Advertiser; held in archival collections at the Library of Congress, loc.gov.
documents.excerpt: We are here this evening to say to those who have mistreated us so long that we are tired — tired of being segregated and humiliated; tired of being kicked about by the brutal feet of oppression... But there will be no crosses burned at any bus stops in Montgomery. There will be no white persons pulled out of their homes and taken out on some distant road and murdered. There will be no threats and intimidation. We will be guided by the highest principles of law and love... One of the great glories of democracy is the right to protest for right. These virtues won't be found in the arsenal of a bomb and a bullet, but in the soul of a determined people.

documents.citation: Excerpt from Bayard Rustin, 'Montgomery Diary,' February 1956, published in Liberation Magazine (1956), and collected in 'Bayard Rustin Papers, Library of Congress (loc.gov)' (public domain, pre-publication rights held by movement archives). Reprinted in The Atlantic, February 1956. Source note: Bayard Rustin, 'Montgomery Diary,' Liberation, February 1956; Library of Congress, Manuscript Division, Bayard Rustin Papers, loc.gov.
documents.excerpt: The economic pinch is working. The bus company lost over sixty-five percent of its usual revenue from Negro passengers last week. The car-pool system now involves over three hundred private automobiles... The spirit here is remarkable. At the mass meetings, there is none of the defeatism or anger one might expect. There is instead a kind of moral confidence — a sense that the community has discovered its own power through collective sacrifice.
